locator.text: Equation (10.23), p. 124, in the proof of Theorem 1.1

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. First equality: stated in Lean only in the general dilation form kineticEnergy (a • u(t, b•x)) t = (‖a‖² · |(b³)⁻¹|) · kineticEnergy u t. Substituting the (10.22) dilation a = √ν, b = ν^{-1/2} (the arguments rescale_candidate passes, with ν > 0) gives ‖a‖² = ν and |(b³)⁻¹| = ν^{3/2}, hence factor ν^{5/2} — exactly the paper's; Lean's kineticEnergy carries a 1/2 that the paper's ‖·‖₂² does not, but it multiplies both sides and cancels, and Lean's time argument comes first. So this half is a faithful general statement awaiting instantiation. Second equality (dissipation): no declaration was found relating ν∫₀¹‖∇u_ν‖₂² dt to ν^{5/2}∫₀¹‖∇u‖₂² dt, or any scaling law for CompactEnergy.dissipation u t = ∑_i ∫ ‖∂_i u(t,x)‖² dx. The Lean takes a different route to the same place: candidate_energy_estimates proves 2ν ∫_{[0,1)} dissipation u ≤ (cumulativeForceNorm f 1)² directly from CandidateProperties at the viscosity ν in question, so the already-rescaled candidate's dissipation is bounded without transporting the viscosity-one bound. CandidateProperties itself carries only energy_bounded (no dissipation clause), and that clause is supplied by the first equality's lemma, so Theorem 1.1 as formalized is unaffected.
